svg.title: Exit status: did the command succeed?
svg.desc: In Bash, every command leaves an exit status. Zero means success; a nonzero result depends on the command, here a false test rather than a malfunction. test -f note.txt checks for a regular file, a file holding contents rather than a directory. status=$? immediately stores the result in a variable, with no spaces around the equals sign, and quoted expansion retrieves it for printf. Independent examples each run their own test and allow the command after double ampersand on zero or double pipe on nonzero. The false branch prints no when the path is absent or another type. Printed text is distinct from status.
svg.text: Exit status = the result value a command reports to the shell.
0 means success. Nonzero depends on the command: a false test here, not a malfunction.
Requires Bash. test -f note.txt: is this a regular file (contents, not a directory)?
status=$? stores the previous result in a variable; no spaces around =.
"$status" inserts its value. Save $? immediately: printf sets a new status.
Independent examples: each runs a new test.
&& / || allow the next command. no: missing or another type. Status is not printed output.
